criteria.criterion: Use the correct FRED series page (UNRATE) and avoid sign-in/subscription actions
criteria.description: Navigate to the FRED 'Unemployment Rate' series page for UNRATE (not a different unemployment series) and use the information shown there. Full credit if the agent clearly uses/targets the UNRATE series page and does not sign in, create an account, or subscribe to notifications. If FRED is inaccessible (e.g., site down, captcha, blocked) but the agent clearly indicates the attempt and the blocking issue, award full credit for this criterion. Partial credit if the agent likely used FRED but does not clearly indicate UNRATE specifically. No credit if the agent uses a different series (even if related) or violates constraints by signing in/subscribing.

criteria.criterion: Record series metadata exactly as displayed
criteria.description: Report the series metadata fields as displayed on the UNRATE page: Units, Frequency, and Seasonal Adjustment (wording must match exactly). Full credit if all three are present and the wording is preserved exactly as shown. If the agent cannot view these fields due to page load/rendering/access issues after attempting to use the UNRATE page, award partial credit if the agent clearly reports the limitation encountered (do not require guessing). Partial credit if one field is missing or wording is paraphrased. No credit if metadata is from another source/series or is clearly incorrect/fabricated.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Screenshots (latest is Screenshot 2) show metadata: “Units: Percent” with “Seasonally Adjusted” displayed directly beneath, and “Frequency: Monthly.”
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: The agent reported the exact displayed wording for units (“Percent”), frequency (“Monthly”), and seasonal-adjustment status (“Seasonally Adjusted”). Although the agent combined units and seasonal adjustment into one bullet and added a comma, the required wording is preserved exactly as displayed. Award full credit.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: In the metadata area above the chart, the screenshot shows: "Units: Percent" with "Seasonally Adjusted" directly below it. It also shows "Frequency: Monthly".
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: All required metadata fields are visible and match the agent’s predicted output wording/casing: Units is "Percent", seasonal-adjustment status is "Seasonally Adjusted", and frequency is "Monthly". The agent combined Units and seasonal adjustment into one bullet but preserved the exact phrases as displayed.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Minor formatting difference only: the agent wrote "Units: Percent , Seasonally Adjusted" with an extra space before the comma; the screenshot displays them as separate lines ("Units: Percent" and "Seasonally Adjusted"). The core wording matches exactly.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: Metadata fields visible on the series page include: “Units: Percent” with “Seasonally Adjusted” shown directly beneath it, and “Frequency: Monthly”.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: All required metadata elements (Units, Frequency, Seasonal Adjustment status) are visible and match what the agent reported. The agent’s formatting combines Units and Seasonal Adjustment as “Percent , Seasonally Adjusted”; the screenshot shows them as two lines (“Units: Percent” and “Seasonally Adjusted”), but the exact wording of each label/value (“Percent”, “Seasonally Adjusted”, “Monthly”) is correct.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Minor formatting discrepancy: the agent output includes an extra space before the comma in “Percent , Seasonally Adjusted” and presents Seasonal Adjustment as appended to Units, whereas the page displays “Seasonally Adjusted” as its own line under Units. The underlying wording matches the screenshot.

dom_model_context.verifier_evidence: DOM-model state 1 (latest) metadata area explicitly displays “Units: Percent , Seasonally Adjusted” and “Frequency: Monthly”. The seasonal-adjustment wording appears embedded in the Units line (as shown), not necessarily as a separate labeled field.

However, the rubric requires a Seasonal Adjustment field/wording to be reported exactly as displayed; in this DOM snapshot there is no distinct "Seasonal Adjustment:" metadata label visible, only the phrase "Seasonally Adjusted" embedded in the Units line. Therefore, the DOM supports the wording "Seasonally Adjusted" but does not support the existence of a separate seasonal-adjustment metadata field as a labeled item.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent-reported metadata in the predicted output collapses units and seasonal adjustment into one bullet ("Units: Percent , Seasonally Adjusted"), which matches the DOM text, but it does not separately report a "Seasonal Adjustment" field as required by the criterion. Also, the predicted output did not preserve the exact spacing/punctuation as shown (DOM shows "Percent , Seasonally Adjusted" with a space before the comma).

criteria.criterion: Record the three latest displayed observation months and values exactly as displayed
criteria.description: Report the three latest observations shown on the UNRATE series page, preserving the month, year, and decimal values exactly as displayed. Full credit if exactly three latest displayed months and their values are correct and match the page display at the time of access. If the observations table/chart cannot be accessed or does not render due to external issues (site down, blocking, dynamic content not loading), award partial credit if the agent clearly reports the issue and what portion (if any) was visible; do not require guessing. Partial credit if fewer than three are provided, if observations are not the latest displayed, or if there are minor transcription errors. No credit if values/months are not from the UNRATE page or are fabricated.

criteria.criterion: Stop after recording metadata and three latest observations
criteria.description: Adhere to the stopping condition by ending the work once the series metadata and three latest displayed observations have been recorded (or once it is clearly established they cannot be retrieved due to access/rendering issues). Full credit if no additional unnecessary steps/data beyond what was asked are included. Partial credit if minor extra, non-conflicting information is added. No credit if the agent continues significantly beyond scope (e.g., reporting long histories, additional series, or other analyses) instead of stopping.
